facts.text: The only player of the 1980s to rush for 600 yards as a quarterback was Randall Cunningham — and he did it twice (1988: 624 rush yds; 1989: 621 rush yds).
The only player of the 1980s to score 150 points: Mark Moseley, 1983 — 161 pts.
The only player of the 1980s to gain 2,500 all-purpose yards: Lionel James, 1985 — 2,535 all-purpose yds.
The only player of the 1980s to catch 100 passes: Art Monk, 1984 — 106 rec.
Only two players of the 1980s threw for 3,600 yards with 17 or fewer touchdowns: Brian Sipe (1981: 3,876 yds, 17 TD); Bernie Kosar (1986: 3,854 yds, 17 TD).
Only two players of the 1980s rushed for 1,800 yards: Eric Dickerson (3×, best 1984: 2,105 yds); Earl Campbell (1980: 1,934 yds).
Only two players of the 1980s gained 1,500 receiving yards: Jerry Rice (1986: 1,570 yds); Roy Green (1984: 1,555 yds).
Only two players of the 1980s posted a passer rating of 100 (250+ attempts): Joe Montana (3×, best 1989: 112.4 rating); Dan Marino (1984: 108.9 rating).
The only player of the 1980s to run for 8 touchdowns as a quarterback: Vince Evans, 1980 — 8 rush TD.
The only player of the 1980s to return 3 kickoffs for touchdowns: Ron Brown, 1985 — 3 KR TD.
The only player of the 1980s to return 3 punts for touchdowns: LeRoy Irvin, 1981 — 3 PR TD.
Only two players of the 1980s threw 33 touchdown passes: Dan Marino (2×, best 1984: 48 TD, 17 INT); Dan Fouts (1981: 33 TD, 17 INT).

Just three players of the 1980s gained 2,200 yards from scrimmage: Marcus Allen (1985: 2,314 scrimmage yds); Eric Dickerson (2×, best 1984: 2,244 scrimmage yds); James Wilder (1984: 2,229 scrimmage yds).
Only two players of the 1980s caught 15 touchdown passes: Jerry Rice (3×, best 1987: 22 rec TD); Mark Clayton (1984: 18 rec TD).
Only two players of the 1980s returned 3 interceptions for touchdowns: Lloyd Burruss (1986: 3 pick-sixes); Ronnie Lott (1981: 3 pick-sixes).

Just four players of the 1980s threw 28 interceptions: Vinny Testaverde (1988: 35 INT, 13 TD); Richard Todd (1980: 30 INT, 17 TD); Lynn Dickey (1983: 29 INT, 32 TD); Ken Stabler (1980: 28 INT, 13 TD).

Just four players of the 1980s gained 1,000 receiving yards on 50 or fewer catches: Flipper Anderson (1989: 1,146 yds on 44 rec); Stanley Morgan (1981: 1,029 yds on 44 rec); Wes Chandler (1982: 1,032 yds on 49 rec); Wesley Walker (1986: 1,016 yds on 49 rec).
Just four players of the 1980s scored 20 touchdowns: John Riggins (1983: 24 TD); Jerry Rice (1987: 23 TD); Joe Morris (1985: 21 TD); Eric Dickerson (1983: 20 TD).

Just four players of the 1980s averaged 5.5 yards a carry (150+ carries): James Brooks (1989: 5.6 ypc on 221); Eric Dickerson (1984: 5.6 ypc on 379); Stump Mitchell (1985: 5.5 ypc on 183); Bo Jackson (1989: 5.5 ypc on 173).
7 players threw for 4,300 yards in the 1980s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Dan Marino, 1984 — 5,084 yds.
9 players carried the ball 370 times in the 1980s (12 seasons). The most extreme: James Wilder, 1984 — 407 carries.
11 players rushed for 1,000 yards at 3.8 a carry or worse in the 1980s (13 seasons). The most extreme: James Wilder, 1984 — 1,544 yds, 3.8 ypc.
5 players gained 1,000 receiving yards as a tight end in the 1980s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Kellen Winslow, 1980 — 1,290 yds, 89 rec.
Most interceptions thrown in a season in the 1980s: Vinny Testaverde, 1988 — 35.
Most catches in a season in the 1980s: Art Monk, 1984 — 106.
Most interceptions in a season in the 1980s: Lester Hayes, 1980 — 13.
Most sacks in a season in the 1980s: Mark Gastineau, 1984 — 22.
Most points scored in a season in the 1980s: Mark Moseley, 1983 — 161.
Most touchdowns in a season in the 1980s: John Riggins, 1983 — 24.
Best yards per carry in a season (150+ carries) in the 1980s: James Brooks, 1989 — 5.6.
Best yards per catch in a season (40+ catches) in the 1980s: Flipper Anderson, 1989 — 26.
Lowest completion percentage by a 3,010-yard passer in the 1980s: Vinny Testaverde, 1988 — 47.6%.
Highest passer rating in a season (250+ attempts) in the 1980s: Joe Montana, 1989 — 112.4.
Most all-purpose yards in a season in the 1980s: Lionel James, 1985 — 2,535.
Most field goals in a season in the 1980s: Ali Haji-Sheikh, 1983 — 35 of 42.
Best punting average in a season (40+ punts) in the 1980s: Rohn Stark, 1985 — 45.9.
Most passing yards in a season in the 1980s: Dan Marino, 1984 — 5,084.
Most touchdown passes in a season in the 1980s: Dan Marino, 1984 — 48.
Most rushing yards in a season in the 1980s: Eric Dickerson, 1984 — 2,105.
Most receiving yards in a season in the 1980s: Jerry Rice, 1986 — 1,570.
11 players caught 70 passes as a running back in the 1980s. The most extreme: Lionel James, 1985 — 86 rec, 1,027 yds.
4 player-seasons of the 1980s ended on between 990 and 999 receiving yards, just shy of 1,000 — among them Mark Clayton (1985), Jeff Chadwick (1986), Dwight Clark (1980).
5 players got sacked 55 times in the 1980s (6 seasons). The most extreme: Randall Cunningham, 1986 — sacked 72 times.
5 players completed 64% of their passes (250+ attempts) in the 1980s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Ken Anderson, 1982 — 70.6% on 309 att.
Exactly one player of the 1980s finished a season with between 990 and 999 rushing yards, just shy of 1,000: Frank Pollard (1985).
Exactly one player of the 1980s finished a season with between 2,990 and 2,999 passing yards, just shy of 3,000: Joe Ferguson (1983).
Exactly one player of the 1980s finished a season with between 3,990 and 3,999 passing yards, just shy of 4,000: Dan Marino (1989).
5 players made 32 field goals in the 1980s. The most extreme: Ali Haji-Sheikh, 1983 — 35-42 FG.
6 players threw 28 touchdown passes and 23 interceptions in the 1980s (8 seasons). The most extreme: Lynn Dickey, 1983 — 32 TD, 29 INT.
7 players averaged 22 yards a catch (30+ catches) in the 1980s (9 seasons). The most extreme: Flipper Anderson, 1989 — 26 per catch, 44 rec.
5 players ran for 18 touchdowns in the 1980s. The most extreme: John Riggins, 1983 — 24 rush TD.
9 players recorded 18 sacks in the 1980s (13 seasons). The most extreme: Mark Gastineau, 1984 — 22 sacks.
17 players fumbled 14 times in the 1980s. The most extreme: Dave Krieg, 1989 — 18 fumbles.
18 players intercepted 9 passes in the 1980s (19 seasons). The most extreme: Lester Hayes, 1980 — 13 INT.
9 players averaged 8.5 yards a pass attempted (200+ attempts) in the 1980s (11 seasons). The most extreme: Lynn Dickey, 1983 — 9.2 Y/A on 484 att.
19 players forced 6 fumbles in the 1980s (20 seasons). The most extreme: Mike Douglass, 1981 — 9 forced.
23 players recover 6 fumbles in the 1980s (27 seasons). The most extreme: Dave Krieg, 1989 — 9 recoveries.

method: NFL before 2000: each line is one Stathead (Pro Football Reference) Season Finder query over the decade, run in a signed-in subscriber session; the result rows, with Pro Football Reference's stable player ids, are stored as provenance. Nothing recalled or estimated.

Passing, rushing and receiving are official from 1932, interceptions from 1940, sacks from 1982; rules on a category a decade did not record simply return nothing. The 1960s include AFL seasons, which NFL records count; the 1940s exclude the AAFC, which they do not.
